..
A broad trough combined with moderate upper-level divergence of the 
Marianas will continue to bring scattered thunderstorms early 
tonight. While the trough will remain, models indicate upper-level 
support will decrease overnight. Moisture will remain in the area
through Thursday but with thunderstorm coverage will likely tapper 
down to isolated. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
Thursday will become isolated through the weekend as more stable air 
moves into the region. Moisture will remain high enough, however, for
island effects showers to be possible for at least Guam over the 
next several days. By late weekend or early next week, model guidance
suggests a new disturbance may develop far south-southeast of the 
Marianas, possibly bringing a new round of unsettled weather by the 
end of the forecast period.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate northeast winds are expected to gradually 
decrease this week. Combined seas are around 4 feet from a decreasing
west-northwest swell and an increasing east swell. Scattered showers
and thunderstorms tonight will become isolated thunderstorms after 
midnight. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will likely 
return Thursday. 

For coastal reefs, a moderate risk of rip currents will continue 
along west-facing reefs. Based on the swells and buoy data, north 
and south-facing reefs are no longer under a moderate risk. East 
facing reefs may reach a moderate risk by Thursday afternoon as an 
east swell builds into the Marianas. A high risk of lightning early 
tonight will become moderate after midnight and persist through 
Thursday.

Eastern Micronesia...
A monsoon trough stretches across much of eastern Micronesia this
afternoon and will promote periods of unsettled weather over the
coming days for all forecast locations. Numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms are expected at Majuro through Thursday with 
conditions then improving slightly Thursday night. Scattered showers
and isolated thunderstorms are expected at Kosrae and Pohnpei 
through Thursday with conditions then deteriorating Thursday night 
as a wet and unsettled weather pattern begins. Numerous showers 
isolated thunderstorms will be possible on Friday and into the 
weekend with locally heavy rainfall possible at both locations. 

Moderate to fresh west to southwest winds are expected to continue at
all forecast points through tonight. Wind will begin to ease 
slightly Thursday at Majuro and Kosrae, becoming mostly moderate at
both sites. Moderate to fresh southwest winds will continue at 
Pohnpei through Friday, easing slightly as we head into the weekend 
to mostly moderate. A Small Craft Advisory remains in effect for the 
coastal waters of Pohnpei through at least Thursday night and at 
Kosrae through at least tonight. Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet will 
continue for the next couple of days with seas consisting of a west 
swell, a northeast swell, and a southerly swell. Locally choppy seas
will be possible at Pohnpei. Headlines were added at Pohnpei and 
Kosrae for elevated surf possible along south-facing reefs at both 
locations and also for west-facing reefs at Pohnpei. 

Western Micronesia...
A ridge remains firmly in place over Palau and Yap regions, and is 
still inducing some diffluent flow, leading to quiet conditions over 
the a day or two. Island-induced showers and thunderstorms are 
possible for Palau during the afternoons for the next few days. 
Overall, a fairly dry pattern is expected to remain through Friday 
night. Then, the monsoon disturbance, that is currently between Chuuk
Lagoon and Guam, is expected to move into the Philippine seas. This 
is may produce showers, bring some much needed rain to Palau and Yap.

A monsoon disturbance, located northwest of Chuuk, is expected to 
move in a general west-northwest direction and remain fairly 
disorganized, however, the strengthening convergence along the 
western and southern peripheries will be the focus of unsettled 
weather for the region through the remainder of the week. As the 
disturbance shifts west-northwestward, scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms are expected to continue through Sunday at Chuuk. 

Current altimetry data shows combined seas have remained relatively
stable at 2 to 4 feet near Palau and Yap, and 3 to 5 feet at Chuuk. 
Benign marine conditions are expected to continue over the next 
several days, with seas increasing to 4 to 6 feet by around Saturday
for Chuuk coastal waters due to an increase in south to southeast 
swell. Light to gentle winds persist over the next several days with 
an increase in gentle to moderate southwesterly winds at Chuuk 
starting Wednesday.
